- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce noise and align with sentiment-weighted trend.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect sentiment mismatch.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model often underestimates upside; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven reversal potential.
